projects.name: Accurate Block Placement
projects.summary: Hold right click with a block and every new spot you look at gets one, however fast you move.
projects.description:
Placing blocks fast is all about timing: vanilla places a block every four ticks while you hold right click, so moving fast skips spots and moving slowly stacks extra blocks. **Accurate Block Placement** times it for you: hold right click and every *new* spot you look at gets a block at once.

- **A new spot, a block**: bridging, building walls and floors, or sweeping along a row; no spot skipped, however fast you move.
- **No extra blocks**: staring at one spot places nothing more.
- **A single click stays a single block**: right after the click it waits as vanilla does, unless you turn the view.
- **Building backwards**: walking backwards while placing toward yourself places one block per step.
- Doors, chests, buttons and other blocks you click still work as usual.

**Settings** (Options > Mods > Accurate Block Placement): turn it on or off, bind a key to toggle it (unbound by default), and choose whether it works on servers.

Some servers see fast, accurate placing as a cheat: check their rules, or turn "Allowed on servers" off.

A port of [Accurate Block Placement: Reborn](https://modrinth.com/mod/accurate-block-placement-reborn) (MIT) by Clayborn, Flourick, schwar and KadTheHunter, rewritten in Rust for Horizon.

projects.name: Applied Energistics 2
projects.summary: Unofficial port of Applied Energistics 2 15.4.12: ME networks, autocrafting, spatial storage and more.
projects.description:
An unofficial port of Applied Energistics 2 15.4.12 to Horizon, not made or endorsed by its authors. Please report problems to this port, not to them.

Rewritten in Rust: ME networks, storage cells, autocrafting, the cable bus with facades, P2P tunnels, spatial storage, the guide and the Fluix Researcher.

**One file, no separate content mod.**

### Optional integrations
Each is compiled in only when its mod is in the same build, so adding or removing JEI or Jade takes effect at the next build.
- **With JEI:** AE2's recipes and information pages, "+" transfer into terminals, and dragging items onto config slots.
- **With Jade:** network state, channels, P2P links, charge, crafting and stored power.

### Missing or not the same
- **No spatial dimension.** Horizon mods can't add one. A player in a spatial cell goes to a walled plot far out in the End, so `/tp` and F3 say `minecraft:the_end`. A swap with a player takes up to about a second.
- **No Java addons.** AE2's Java API isn't available, and the integrations work only with the Horizon ports of JEI and Jade.
- **Two storage buses on one inventory:** only the first reaches it.
- **Moving items** costs power through terminals, interfaces, export buses and wireless terminals. An IO port and the crafting terminal's refills pay nothing yet.
- **Power** is judged once a second, so a network with too little goes down at the next look and comes back after about 40 ticks, where AE2's is at once and 32.
- **Unformed crafting, quantum and spatial blocks** join a network before they're formed.
- **Autocrafting gaps:** a pattern input of more than one is a single template, so some plans report items missing that AE2 would find. Blocking mode looks at all six sides, provider priority is ignored, and a machine's request for more than it can make crafts nothing.
- **Other differences:** machines have 6 or 4 orientations rather than 24, menus are in English, fluix tools are diamond tools, and guide scenes have no annotations.
- **Crafting ETA is an estimate:** 1.1% off on average on the test rig, 2.0% at worst.
- **Nested P2P error** is an approximation.
- **World height:** parts on cables assume -64 to 319.

The Fluix Researcher and its trades rely on mixins, so they are the part most likely to break on a Horizon update.

### Tested
Tested on Horizon commit 6475f62, on Windows, in single player, on LAN with one guest, and on a dedicated server with one client, including attacks by a non-operator with a modified client. This version is built for Horizon commit 66f3981, where AE2 alone compiles but hasn't been run, and the JEI and Jade integrations haven't been compiled. Other platforms, more than one guest, pipes from other mods and speed against the Java mod were not tested.

### Known issue
In some test runs, placing a part into a cable cell did nothing. It isn't one specific part, and it's probably lost test clicks, but that isn't proven.

Textures and models are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: noncommercial use only.

projects.name: Astral Cruiser
projects.summary: A huge pilotable starship with a walkable interior, lasers, dash and live portals between dimensions.
projects.description:
A huge starship you fly yourself, with a large walkable interior that moves with it.

- **Flight:** WASD with the ship following your view, and F5 views including the ship's own.
- **Weapons:** turrets, nose guns and two beams.
- **Travel:** coordinate dash and jump. Long dashes show only a small strip of far terrain around the ship.
- **Portals:** a portal shows the real destination dimension live, and you cross it aboard or on foot.
- **Start:** `/astral spawn`, then `/astral board`. N opens the control panel; keys are in Options > Mods > Settings.

**What it does as a native mod.** It is compiled into the game with no sandbox. It changes the game's rendering, ticking and chunk loading for the ship and portals, and registers a thread-exit callback in builds made with MinGW so the allocator frees finished threads' memory.

**What it does not do.** It adds no network access of its own beyond the game's own, and it reads no accounts or files outside the game's data. It keeps the ship in the world's own folder (`astral_cruiser/ship.json`). It holds no Minecraft code or assets.

Weapons hurt the mobs they hit. With blasting turned on in the control panel (off by default), the nose guns and beams also blow up the blocks they hit. Portals can hang in the air, so a player on foot falls if there is no ground at the exit, including into the End's void.

Built for this Horizon commit only: `68ac6f647e7022b2c696e81863d7cface28c9416`.

projects.name: Atlas
projects.summary: A clone of Xaero's Minimap and World Map: a sharp minimap, a world map of everywhere you've been, and waypoints.
projects.description:
![Atlas in the game](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MrCloudy2/horizon-atlas/main/docs/images/hero.jpg)

Atlas is meant to be a close copy of Xaero's Minimap and Xaero's World Map for Horizon: the same look, the same keys and the same settings. The minimap, the world map and the waypoints share one map of the world, kept on disk per world, server and dimension.

- **Minimap**: drawn at your screen's resolution, turns with you, with entity dots that fade with height. Hold Tab for mob faces, player faces and item icons.
- **World map (M)**: drag and zoom. B makes a waypoint under the pointer.
- **Map modes**: Auto (the surface in the open, the cave around you under a roof), Cave and Layer.
- **Waypoints (U, B, H)**: sets, filter, Share, Teleport for operators, deathpoints, temporary waypoints, and labels in the world.
- **Overlays**: chunk grid, light overlay, slime chunks (with `/atlas seed`).
- **Settings (Y)**: pages of options with search; `/atlas` sets exact values.

![The minimap, with faces while Tab is held](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MrCloudy2/horizon-atlas/main/docs/images/minimap-tab.png)

![The world map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MrCloudy2/horizon-atlas/main/docs/images/world-map.jpg)

**What it does and doesn't do.** Atlas reads the world your client already has and draws on your screen. It writes only its own folder, `horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/atlas/` (settings, waypoints and maps). It opens no network connections. It sends something to the server only when you click Teleport (a `/tp` command, for operators) or Share (a chat message with the waypoint).

Atlas is its own code. It copies the look and features of Xaero's mods, but no code or art comes from them, and it isn't made or endorsed by Xaero. Built on Waypoints by Nirokx (MIT); the map columns follow Horizon's minimap (MIT).

Checked on Horizon Nightly 2026-11-05 (`66f3981`). It reads the game's world directly, so a much newer Nightly may need a new release. Turn off Horizon's own Minimap to avoid two maps.

projects.name: ayynoxs map pack
projects.summary: Minimap and full-screen world map with waypoints, cave layers and opt-in map sharing between players.
projects.description:
A **minimap** and a **full-screen world map** for Horizon, written from scratch as a native mod. Inspired by the well-known Java map mods, but no code or graphics are taken from them.

## ayynoxs minimap
- Built on Horizon's own minimap renderer, with coordinates and facing direction below it
- Square or round, north-up or rotating, 4 sizes, zoom with `I` / `O`
- **Waypoints:** `B` opens a window for the name, `Backspace` removes the one you aim at. They show on the minimap, on the world map and in the world with their distance in metres.
- Automatic death point
- Chat commands: `/wp add|del|rename|share|sync|list|clear|help`

## ayynoxs world map
- Full-screen map on `M`: drag or WASD to pan, wheel to zoom
- Drawn like a vanilla map item, one block per cell
- Saves every chunk you explore, per world/server, dimension and layer
- Same layers as the minimap: the surface outside, your head height in caves and in the Nether

## Sharing (off by default)
- `/wp share <nr> <player>` sends a waypoint as a private message, on any server. Only private messages to you can add waypoints.
- Live map sharing is **off by default** and chosen per server with `/wp sync on|off`. When on, explored chunks and new waypoints go to the other players who turned it on, through a Horizon host (co-op/LAN, Horizon servers) or the AyynoxsMapSync plugin on Paper servers.
- What arrives is limited: only your current level, within 2048 blocks of you, at most 1000 waypoints per world.

Languages: English (default), Deutsch, Français, Italiano, Русский.

## What it does and doesn't
- **Hooks:** the native hook points (frame, tick, HUD, keys, commands, minimap, settings, mods list, screen keys and characters, mod messages, player join/leave), plus the Advancements screen's draw, mouse, scroll and close (the world map is drawn in its place), `extras_connecting` (the server address, for the map's folder) and the chat HUD's `add` / `add_signed` (to hide shared-waypoint private messages).
- **Files:** writes only under `horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/ayynoxs_minimap/` (settings, waypoints) and `ayynoxs_worldmap/` (map tiles).
- **Network:** no internet access. It only sends Horizon mod messages on `ayynoxs_map:sync` to the server you play on (shares only after `/wp sync on`), and `/msg` commands you start yourself with `/wp share <nr> <player>`.
- Pinned to nightly `6475f62` (2026-11-04).

versions.changelog:
Changes from the review of 0.4.1:
- Map sharing is off by default and chosen per server: /wp sync on (or the setting) turns it on. When a server can pass shares on, the pack says so once in chat.
- Waypoints arrive only through private messages to the player (commands.message.display.incoming); the marker in public chat does nothing.
- Shared chunks are taken only for the player's current level, a real layer and within 2048 blocks of the player; shared waypoints stop at 1000 per world.
Also: the world map is drawn like a map item again (one block per cell), which is cheaper while dragging.

projects.name: Baritone
projects.summary: A Rust port of the Baritone pathfinder: #goto, #mine, #farm, #build, #explore, #follow, #elytra and the rest.
projects.description:
A port to Rust of Baritone 1.21.4 for Horizon, written from the Java source: the pathfinder (A* with walking, sprinting, parkour, bridging, pillaring, doors, ladders and water bucket landings), `#goto`, `#mine`, `#farm`, `#follow`, `#explore`, `#build` (schematics and shapes), `#tunnel`, `#elytra`, waypoints, and every setting and command of the Java mod. Type `#help` in chat. PARITY.md in the source lists every Java class and what became of it.

What it does not do: it draws the cached chunks semitransparent (`renderCachedChunks`) only if Horizon later offers a renderer for it. Like the Java mod it plays for you, so many multiplayer servers ban it: that choice is the player's.

For reviewers:
- No network access of its own: nothing in the source opens a socket or an HTTP request.
- It writes only its settings, cached chunks and waypoints under `horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/baritone/`, and reads the schematic and explore-filter files the player names in a command.
- It starts an operating system program in two places, both in `src/utils/notification.rs`: desktop notifications (PowerShell on Windows, osascript on macOS, notify-send on Linux), which are off unless the player sets `desktopNotifications true`, and `#pizza`, which opens a web page in the browser (the Java mod has the same command).
- The `.hnmod` is built from the source of the tagged release, `python tools/pack.py`, and is the same file every time.
- Pinned to Nightly 2026-11-04 (6475f62): the launcher builds the game on that commit, and so does not depend on the Nightly the player has.

projects.name: Chop!
projects.summary: Cut one log and the whole tree tips over, crashes down and breaks apart, with soft vanilla sounds and particles.
projects.description:
Cut one log with an axe: the whole tree tips over like a real falling tree, crashes to the ground, and breaks apart from the base to the top in little pops. Everything is made of vanilla sounds and particles: no resource pack.

- **The log shakes while you cut it**, then pops when it gives way.
- **A physical fall**: the trunk drops onto the stump, creaks, tips over with gravity and stops where it meets the ground. Leaves in the way are crushed.
- **Falls in front of you**, within an adjustable angle, toward the clearest side.
- **A cute break-up** from the base to the top, with clouds, sparkles and hearts.
- **Replants a sapling** of the tree's kind (from its loot, or always).
- **Chain reactions**: a falling trunk can knock over the next tree.
- **Adjustable damage**: hurts monsters by default; animals, allies and players are spared unless you turn them on.
- Vanilla loot (Fortune, Silk Touch), honest axe wear, fall preview, shaking trees with an empty hand, giant mushrooms and Nether fungi, angry bees, birds, apples, biome-tinted leaves, optional loot into your inventory.
- **Everything is configurable in game**, with commands or by clicking in the chat: `/chop config` (operators), `/chop perso` (each player's sounds, particles and preview), `/chop stats`, `/chop aide`. The menus are in French.

**What it does and doesn't do.** It runs server-side, where the world runs: players who join install nothing. No network access, no telemetry, never runs a program. It reads and writes one file, `<world>/data/chop.txt` (settings, stats, player-placed logs). It only touches trees, the sapling it replants, its own `block_display` entities and what a falling tree hits. Besides the game's functions, it runs a few vanilla commands as the server: `kill` on its own tagged displays, `item modify` for the axe's wear, `damage` on a player the tree hits (off by default), and `summon item` / `setblock … keep` for loot and replanting when the tree is in another dimension.

The launcher builds a separate game with it, and it runs with your account's permissions. Each version is pinned to one Horizon Nightly and Horizon Mixins revision, named in its changelog; the launcher builds those exact revisions.

Original mod by Mayonesu0. All rights reserved, except the grants in its [LICENSE](https://github.com/Mayonesu0/chop/blob/main/LICENSE): players may use it unchanged, Horizon's registry may distribute it, and Horizon's reviewers may read it to review it.

## Controls

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Hold **V** | Zoom in 3x |
| Scroll while holding V | Zoom from 1x to 10x, x1.1 per wheel step |
| Release V | Back to normal view at once |

While V is held, the mouse wheel zooms instead of switching hotbar slots, and turning slows down in step with the zoom so aiming stays steady. Rebind the key on the mod's page in Options > Mods.

## How it differs from Horizon's own Zoom

| | Horizon Zoom | Classic Zoom |
|---|---|---|
| Default key | Z | V |
| Starting zoom | 4x (configurable) | 3x |
| Range | 1.25x to 10x | 1x to 10x |
| Wheel step | x1.25 | x1.1, finer |
| Transition | Smooth by default | Instant |
| Settings page | Yes | None |

Both can be installed at once: they use different keys.

- Horizon caps zoom at 10x, so there is no 50x as in WI Zoom.
- Written from scratch for Horizon's mod API. Not affiliated with Wurst-Imperium.

projects.summary: Build rotating machines and small factories in Horizon with gears, belts, presses and fans.
projects.description:
An unofficial, experimental Rust port of [Create](https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create), made by Delete228. It is not made or endorsed by the Create team; their original code is MIT and is credited in the mod's NOTICE.

- Drive machines with water wheels, hand cranks or a Creative Motor.
- Route power through shafts, gears, gearboxes, clutches and encased chain drives.
- Move items on basic belts and depots. Press sheets, mill ingredients, mix in a Basin or process items with a fan.

projects.name: Cross Version
projects.summary: Allows version hopping offline.
projects.description:
Join servers that speak an older Minecraft protocol from Horizon (which speaks only 26.3's), as a native
mod.

When you join, it asks the server which version it speaks. If it isn't 26.3, it starts a
[ViaProxy](https://github.com/ViaVersion/ViaProxy) on a loopback port and sends the join through it: the proxy speaks
26.3 to Horizon and the server's own version to the server. A join to a 26.3 server starts nothing.

- **Offline-mode servers only**: online-mode servers can't be joined.
- The server list shows such servers as joinable, with their own version, instead of "Incompatible version!".
- **Edit Server** and **Direct Connect** get a line to choose the version yourself (auto, 1.8 to 1.21.4, 26.3), for
  servers whose status reports the wrong one.
- Needs Java 17 or later on your computer. On first use it downloads ViaProxy (GPL-3.0), checked against a SHA-256
  pinned in its source.

projects.name: Daybreak
projects.summary: Sun shadows, reflective water, waving plants, coloured light, sun rays and bloom, built to cost as little GPU time as possible.
projects.description:
Daybreak is a shader pack in Horizon's own format. It runs inside Horizon's renderer, so Horizon's culling, batching and LOD stay in charge, and it adds as little GPU time as it can.

- Sun and moon shadows with smooth edges
- Warm sunlight, blue sky light in the shade, a dim blue night
- Coloured block light: soul fire blue, redstone red, copper green, froglights
- Light from torches in your hand (turn on Horizon's Dynamic lights in Extras)
- Waving leaves, grass, flowers and crops
- Water with waves, reflections, refraction and the sun's glint
- A deeper sky with warm sunsets, sun rays, sun glare and haze
- Mobs take the sun's shadow; the Nether and the End get their own light

Every effect can be changed or turned off in the game: Options > Horizon Settings > Shader Packs > Shader Options. The quality is yours to pick there too: turn shadows off for the least GPU time, or choose the shadow map's detail (1024 to 4096) and distance (64 to 160 blocks). The defaults are soft shadows over 96 blocks with water reflections.

Original code, no Minecraft assets. Source: https://github.com/hildlabs/horizon-shaders

versions.changelog: One pack instead of four: shadows on/off, shadow detail (1024/2048/4096) and shadow distance (64/96/160 blocks) are now options on the Lighting page. The defaults match the old High pack; the Low, Medium and Ultra packs are gone. Needs a Horizon Nightly from 2026-11-05 or newer.

First release: sun and moon shadows, warm sunlight and blue shade, coloured block light, waving plants, reflective water with waves, a deeper sky, sun rays, sun glare, haze, bloom and a colour grade. The High preset (soft shadows over 96 blocks, water reflections). Needs a Horizon build from 2026-11-03 or newer (Nightly 2944480 and later). Release v0.1.1 of the repository.

projects.name: Distant Horizons for Horizon Client
projects.summary: See far past your render distance: Distant Horizons' level-of-detail terrain, ported to Rust as a native mod.
projects.description:
An unofficial Rust port of [Distant Horizons](https://gitlab.com/distant-horizons-team/distant-horizons) by James Seibel and contributors: the world past your render distance, drawn at lower detail the farther it is.

- Far terrain built from the chunks you visit, and in single player from the world generator, out to 64–1024 chunks.
- Detail drops with distance by Distant Horizons' own rule, with its five quality presets.
- LODs are kept on disk per world, so they load at once next time.
- Drawn by Horizon's far-terrain renderer with block textures and biome tints.

Settings: Options > Mods > Distant Horizons. In chat: `/dh` for status, `/dh distance 512`, `/dh quality high`, `/dh debug on` and more (Tab completes them).

Native source mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page, press Build there and confirm the native-code warning. The launcher downloads its own Rust and builds a separate game (10–30 minutes the first time). It runs with your account's permissions.

Pinned to Horizon nightly `d009ebd140476b5bdc958c00f56a75e82abec691` (2026-10-29) and Horizon Mixins `0d6b103c70633d8fd9443d8d0acd3aadaacedb06`; the launcher builds these exact revisions. Other Horizon revisions have not been validated. It builds together with Horizon's official native mods; it can't be built with a native mod pinned to a different Horizon commit. Turn Video Settings > LOD Distance off: Horizon's own far terrain draws in the same place.

Known limits: heavy at 256+ chunks (about 30–40 fps on an Apple M5 MacBook Pro); water at LOD edges can show see-through walls.

LGPL-3.0, as Distant Horizons; its copyright notices are kept. Not made or endorsed by the Distant Horizons team. No Minecraft code or assets are included. Ported by Deniz Şahin with Claude (Anthropic).

versions.changelog: First release: pinned to Horizon nightly d009ebd and Horizon Mixins 0d6b103.

projects.summary: Reduce resource usage while Minecraft is in the background, idle, or on battery
projects.description:
Dynamic FPS for Horizon: it lowers the frame rate, and optionally the volume, while the game window is in the background, hovered but not focused, minimised or idle, or while Horizon's battery mode is on.

- Caps by default: 30 FPS hovered, 10 unfocused (after half a second), 1 minimised, 20 after a minute idle, 30 on battery; no cap while you play.
- At 1 FPS the game still runs its input, network and ticks up to 20 times a second.
- Volume lowering is off by default.
- Settings: `config/dynamic-fps-for-rust.json` in the game folder, written with the defaults on first start. There is no settings screen yet.

An independent implementation after the public description of Dynamic FPS; it holds none of its code. It changes no shared game settings and has no network access.

While you eat food, or drink a potion or milk, the item in your hand shows its bitten frames as you go.

The frame pack can be the one `tools/make_frame_pack.py` makes from the original EatingAnimation download.

projects.name: ElytraTrails
projects.summary: A Horizon mod that adds elytra trails with additional features.
projects.description:
A native mod for Horizon. The idea comes from [ElytraTrails](https://github.com/dbrighthd/elytratrails) by dbrighthd.

What it does

Lines stream from the outer tip of each wing while you glide and fade out over time. Only players get trails.

- Colors: ice, gold, rose, violet, white, rainbow, or speed (cold blue when slow, orange and thicker when fast).
- Patterns: solid, dashed or wavy. Built in only.
- Pulse: gently breathing brightness.
- Night: lines are brighter at night and dimmer in the day.
- Boost: a sudden speed jump, such as a firework, lights the whole trail up for two seconds.
- Formation: gliding players close to each other are joined by white lines between their wingtips.
- Lines taper toward the tail, the wingtip has a soft glow, and fading eases in and out.
- Singleplayer: without LAN or a server, all code for other players is skipped.
- Sharing: your color and pattern are sent through the server, so other players see them (single player, LAN and servers). (Untested, I don't have friends)

Settings

Open Options > Mods > ElytraTrails:

- **Trails**: turns every line on or off.
- **Your trail**: your own lines.
- **Your trail in first person**: on by default. Turn it off to see your lines only in third person (F5).
- **Other players' trails**: the lines of other players within 48 blocks.
- **Color**: see the list above.
- **Duration**: how long a line lasts, 1 to 12 seconds (default 5).
- **Width**: thin, normal or wide.
- **Pattern**: solid, dashed or wavy.
- **Pulse**: on or off.
- **Day/night brightness**: off by default (same brightness at any time). On: lines are brighter at night and dimmer in the day.
- **Optimization** (submenu):
  - **Your wings**: dynamic (the lines follow the real wing movement) or fixed (the line is computed once when gliding starts and then only moves with your body, which is cheaper).
  - **Other players' wings**: dynamic or fixed, the same for other players.
  - **Line detail**: full or half (half draws every second segment, about half the lines).
  - **Other players' range**: 24, 48 or 96 blocks.
  - **Formation lines**: on or off.
  - **Boost flash**: on or off.

## Credits

- ElytraTrails by [dbrighthd](https://github.com/dbrighthd/elytratrails) (MPL-2.0), the original mod. The idea of wing trails comes from it.
- This is a separate implementation for Horizon, written from scratch in Rust. It does not contain code from the original mod.

License

MIT. See LICENSE.

projects.name: Fence Perch
projects.summary: Jump onto fences, walls and closed gates from a standstill, stand on top, step off.
projects.description:
Jump onto fences, walls and closed fence gates from a standstill, stand on top, and step off either side.

### Features
- Walk up to a fence, wall or closed fence gate and jump while stepping forward: you land on top, no run-up needed.
- Stand on it, walk along a connected line, then step off on either side.
- Gates stay closed, so animals stay in the pen while you climb in and out.

### How it works
For the player only, supported barriers collide like a one-block-high block instead of one and a half. Your jump is not stronger: a 1.5-block ledge stays out of reach and low ceilings still block you. On top of a barrier you stand half a block lower than on a full post. Animals, mobs, open gates and all other blocks keep their normal collision.

Supported: vanilla blocks whose IDs end in `_fence`, `_wall` or `_fence_gate` (gates only while closed).

### Multiplayer
The host's server checks movement with the same barrier shape, so the mod works in single-player and on LAN games hosted with it. Every player needs the mod. Joining a world or server without it, and dedicated servers, are not supported.

### Compatibility
For Minecraft 26.3. Each version is built and gameplay-tested on one exact Horizon Nightly; the launcher warns when a newer Nightly breaks it. Tested revisions and results: [Validation](https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-fence-perch/blob/main/VALIDATION.md).

This is a native mod: install only if you trust its source and accept the launcher's native-code warning.

[Watch the demo](https://youtu.be/MNl9MMPWeIY) · [Installation](https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-fence-perch/blob/main/docs/installation.md)

projects.name: FreeCam
projects.summary: Free camera, F6 follow view and nine tripod positions for Horizon.
projects.description:
## FreeCam by Yannis_

Free flight, a high and wide follow view, and nine tripod positions — now native to Horizon.

### Controls

- **F4:** toggle free camera. Move with your movement keys, Jump/Sneak and Sprint. Mouse look is independent of the player.
- **F6:** follow your player while continuing to play normally. The crosshair is hidden while following. Toggle again to restore your previous camera.
- **Hold F4 + 1–9:** save or return to a tripod for the current world.
- **Options → Mods → FreeCam:** rebind keys and adjust camera speed, follow distance and height. Default follow distance: 28 blocks; height: 18 blocks.

### Original Modrinth project

This is the native Rust edition of [FreeCam by Yannis_ on Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/mod/freecam_yannis_) (project ID: `zHbMgWKx`). Use the Modrinth edition with Java/Fabric and this native edition with Horizon. Both use the same existing FreeCam artwork.

The Java edition originated from [MinecraftFreecam/Freecam](https://github.com/MinecraftFreecam/Freecam) and its contributors. Original MIT notices are retained in the repository and bundle. This is an independently maintained port, not an official release of MinecraftFreecam or Horizon.

### Compatibility and scope

For Minecraft 26.3 and Horizon commit `2ebf00a0281c592f79191e76fce0e7d522c6f425`. Two internal hooks provide independent mouse look and player-body visibility, so this release requires that pinned Horizon revision.

The camera only shows chunks already loaded around the player. Free flight passes through blocks and suppresses player movement input and block interactions; follow mode leaves player controls active. World unload and disconnect clear camera state.

No networking, telemetry, background threads, obstruction hiding, block scanning or chunk rebuilding. Settings use Horizon’s local storage. Optional Java collision, fullbright, fog and hand-display settings are not included in this first port.

### Validation

13 distinct core/adapter tests, the full Horizon native build check, and official package validation pass. GitHub CI also passes. Interactive Horizon-world testing and performance measurements remain pending; this is a preview release. [Validation details](https://github.com/yan6678yan-design/freecam-horizon/blob/main/VALIDATION.md).

Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft.

projects.summary: Full 6DOF flight physics and immersive gyro camera tilt for Minecraft Horizon, inspired by Do a Barrel Roll.
projects.description:
**Fly an elytra like an aircraft.** Gyro swaps Horizon's locked horizon for full six-degree-of-freedom control: bank into a roll, pull through it to carve a turn, push the nose past vertical and loop. Inspired by the feel of the Java mod *Do a Barrel Roll*, written from scratch on Horizon's native hook points.

| While gliding | What it does |
|---|---|
| Mouse left / right | Roll — a full 360° with no snap-back |
| Mouse up / down | Pitch through your current bank, so a wing-down pull carves a turn |
| `A` / `D` | Rudder yaw for fine heading corrections |

In third person your avatar, elytra and held item stay pinned to the camera while the world, sky and entities roll around you. When you stop gliding, the view eases back to level and the mouse is an ordinary camera again. Everything else stays vanilla — no keybinds, no config, no setup, just one row in **Options > Mods**.

**What it actually touches.** Client-side camera matrices and the player's own model only. There is no network, filesystem or process access anywhere in the source, no server hooks and no server component; the server never hears about the roll. It declares `hooks: 3`, so the launcher builds it on any Horizon whose native hook API is ≥ 3 rather than one pinned commit. Built and tested against Horizon `ba6344a` with horizon-mixins `d9c83d70`. projects.name: Horizonmatica
projects.summary: Litematica for Horizon: schematics as ghost blocks, a verifier, material lists and a printer that builds the missing blocks for you.
projects.description:
Horizonmatica is a re-creation of **Litematica** (with its **printer**) for Horizon. Load a schematic, see it as ghost blocks in your world, check your build against it, get a material list, and let the printer place the missing blocks.

## Features
- **Formats:** `.litematic` (versions 1–7, several regions), `.schem` (Sponge v1–v3: WorldEdit, FAWE, Amulet, Axiom), `.schematic` (MCEdit / WorldEdit up to 1.12) and vanilla structure `.nbt`. Older files are upgraded with Horizon's data fixer, the same way old worlds are.
- **Overlay:** missing blocks as translucent real block models (chests, banners, heads and other block entities included), optionally visible through walls.
- **Verifier:** wrong block (red), wrong state (orange), extra block (pink), plus a progress HUD.
- **Layers:** all / one layer / above / below / range.
- **Placements:** several at once; move, rotate, mirror, show or hide each; a move mode for mouse wheel and arrow keys. The placements are remembered per world and dimension and restored when you join again.
- **Save your own:** select an area with the selection tool (a stick: left and right click set the corners, the wheel grows and moves the box) and save it as a `.litematic` (blocks and their states), chunk by chunk as in Litematica: chunks not loaded yet show as frames to fly to.
- **Material list:** missing, total and carried, with item icons, in the HUD or in the menu, and copied to the clipboard as a table for spreadsheets.
- **Menu (M):** a screen of its own, drawn with the game's widgets.
- **Pick block:** middle-click a ghost block to take that block in hand, for building by hand.
- **Highlights:** mark missing and wrong blocks through everything, however far away, for all items or just one you pick in the material list.
- **Printer:** places one missing block within reach every few ticks, from the bottom up. It only clicks when Horizon's own placement logic says the click produces exactly the wanted state (stairs, slabs, logs, furnaces…). Redstone-aware order, repeater, comparator and note block setup after placing, double slabs and stacks, chests, falling blocks. The camera never moves.

Usage: put schematics into `schematics/` next to `options.txt` of your instance (`/hm folder` shows the path), then `/hm load <name>` or press **M**. All commands and keys are in the [README](https://github.com/keksi2k/horizonmatica#usage).

## What it does and doesn't do
- **Reads** only files in the instance's `schematics/` folder, and creates that folder if it's missing.
- **Writes** only the `.litematic` files you save (`/hm save`), into that folder. Settings and remembered placements go through Horizon's mod settings.
- **Network:** no connections of its own. The only thing sent to a server is what the printer does: the same block-placing clicks a player would make (with the matching look direction), and hotbar slot changes.
- **"Open folder"** in the menu opens the schematics folder in your file manager through Horizon's own function.
- No telemetry, no downloads, no code run from schematic files. Schematics are parsed as data only.

⚠️ On other people's servers, automatic placing may break the rules or trip anti-cheat. The printer is off until you turn it on (`K` or `/hm printer on`). Its *air place* option (off by default) is noticed by anti-cheat plugins such as Grim.

**Version:** native mods use game internals, so Horizonmatica is pinned to one Horizon commit (currently Nightly 2026-11-04, `67dad0d`). A new Nightly needs a new release.

## Credits
The idea, the way it's used, the file format and the behaviour come from **[Litematica](https://github.com/maruohon/litematica)** by masa (maruohon), maintained by **[Sakura-Ryoko](https://github.com/sakura-ryoko/litematica)**, and from **[Litematica Printer](https://github.com/aleksilassila/litematica-printer)** by aleksilassila. Horizonmatica is not an official project of these authors, isn't made or endorsed by them, and contains none of their code. Only the file format and the behaviour are re-created. If you like it, go and support the originals.

Menus built with [horizon-menus](https://github.com/keksi2k/horizon-menus). MIT licensed.

projects.name: HUD+
projects.summary: One fully configurable HUD with a drag-and-drop editor and four views per module.
projects.description:
HUD+ is one configurable HUD for Horizon, with an in-game drag-and-drop layout editor.

Every module has four views: **Minimal**, **Compact**, **Standard** and **Full**. `Standard` follows the module's own switches; the other three are presets. A profile picks a view for all modules: Minimal gives Minimal, PvP gives Compact, the rest give Standard.

- **AppleSkin** — the original mod's look: golden saturation outlines over the hunger icons and the food/saturation a held item would restore flashing on the same bar. Minimal draws the outlines only, Compact adds food numbers, Full adds saturation, exhaustion, regeneration and the item preview.
- **Effects** — names, amplifiers, remaining time, sorting, grouping, an expiring-only filter and warning colours; can hide vanilla's icons. Minimal shows three rows of icons only, Compact adds names and time up to six rows, Full shows everything without a limit.
- **Inventory, armour and held items** — the whole inventory, hotbar, armour and offhand, stack counts, durability bars or percentages, the selected slot, arrows and totems. Minimal is the hotbar alone, Compact adds counts and a durability bar, Full adds the grid, armour, offhand and empty slots.
- **Coordinates** — XYZ, facing and yaw, chunk, dimension, and the same place in the other dimension. Minimal is XYZ, Compact adds facing, Full adds chunk, dimension, the Nether equivalent and yaw.
- **Keystrokes** — WASD, space, sneak, sprint, mouse buttons and CPS. Minimal is WASD, Compact adds the mouse, Full adds space, sneak, sprint and CPS.
- **Performance and time** — FPS, frame time, 1% low, world clock and day, local time and date, speed. Minimal is FPS, Compact adds the clock, Full adds frame time, the 1% low, real time and speed.
- **Player vitals, food tooltips, durability tooltips.** Minimal is health, Compact adds food and bars, Full adds absorption, armour, air and XP.
- **The vanilla HUD** — every widget (crosshair, hotbar, health and hunger, XP, effect icons, boss bars, chat, scoreboard and the rest) can be moved and scaled on a `Vanilla` page in the editor.

Settings open as one compact, scrollable panel on the right: General, every module, Vanilla HUD and tooltips are on a single screen, the world stays visible, and each module has its view, anchor, scale, background, border and module-specific options inline. Five profiles (Default, Minimal, PvP, Builder, Streamer) and six themes set everything at once. `H` opens the layout editor, `N` settings, `V` the vanilla layout page; `/hudplus on|off|layout|settings|reset|profile|theme` also work. Configuration lives in `config/hud_plus.json`.

HUD+ only draws. It has no network code, no packets, no second process and no movement, attack or use calls; `check_client_only.py` scans every source for them and CI fails the build if one appears. A wire-level audit (`tools/packet_audit.py`) records a stock Horizon client and the HUD+ build on the same fresh server behind a decoding proxy, and the two captures match packet for packet. The mod is compiled into the client (not a file in `mods/`), and a client-only HUD is never named in `horizon:mod_list`. It is provided as is under the MIT licence, without warranty; players are responsible for checking that a server's rules allow the modules they turn on.

Native mod: the launcher builds it into the game on the pinned Horizon Nightly. Uses the saturation art of [squeek502/AppleSkin](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin) (Unlicense).

Also adds an Off setting for effect timers and a separate inventory-grid switch (Minimal keeps only the hotbar), tightens the held/armour rows for the compact views, drops the full-screen sleep overlay from the Vanilla page because there is nothing to move or scale in it, and makes snap-to-grid move modules around their own default offset so dragging one back restores its exact default position.

projects.name: JEI for Horizon
projects.summary: An item and recipe viewer for Horizon: every item beside container screens, with search, recipes, uses, tooltips and bookmarks
projects.description:
An item and recipe viewer for [Horizon](https://playhorizon.dev), the Rust reimplementation of Minecraft: Java Edition.

Horizon JEI is inspired by [JustEnoughItems (JEI)](https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems). JEI serves as the reference specification, while this project is a completely new Rust implementation built around Horizon's native hook points.

**Version 0.2.1 — Overlay and bookmarks**

### Features

- **Recipe Navigation:** Browse recipe history with **Back** and click recipe slots to open the corresponding item.
- **Recipe Placement:** Use the **+** button to place a recipe into the open crafting grid, provided it is available in the recipe book.
- **Item Giving:** Give items through Options → Mods → JEI or `/jei give`. In creative mode, left-click gives one item and right-click gives a full stack. In survival mode, clicking opens the recipe viewer instead.
- **Item Tooltips:** Every tooltip the game shows, the panel's included, names the keys and counts exactly: `R: Recipes (12)`, `U: Uses (3)`, and a star on the stacks in your bar.
- **Subtypes:** Every `(item, components)` pair the recipe tables name is an item of its own in the list, so the potions and the tipped arrows are there like JEI's subtypes.
- **Bookmarks:** Press **A** over a stack to bookmark it. The bar sits at the screen's top left corner in two columns of twelve: the left button opens a bookmark's recipes, the right one its uses, shift-click or the middle button removes it, and dragging moves it. It is kept in `config/jei/bookmarks.txt` and returns with the next world.
- **List Order & Config:** By name or by id, from the settings page or `/jei sort name|id`, kept in `config/jei/jei.cfg` along with the tooltip hints and the bar.
- **World Transition Fix:** Session cache is properly invalidated on world transitions even when JEI is temporarily disabled, preventing stale item IDs or recipes from lingering across worlds.
- **Localization:** English and Spanish interface translations. Item names are retrieved directly from the game and respect the player's language.
- **Diagnostics:** `/jei` reports the game's recipe table sizes, `/jei bookmarks clear` empties the bar and `/jei config` says where its files are.

### Current Limitations

Container slot click integration (R and U work over any slot, a click does not), the creative inventory panel, the non-recipe categories (anvil, grindstone, composter, and fuel), shift-click recipe placement, recipe transfer into furnaces, and the `$tooltip` / `%creative tab` searches are not yet supported.

Some of these features require native hook points that Horizon does not currently expose. See the [JEI parity matrix](https://github.com/enderliker/horizon-jei/blob/main/docs/jei-parity.md) for implementation details.

### Requirements & Security

Requires Horizon **26.3** and hook points version **313** or later: tested and verified on Horizon Nightly (`6560641` and latest `fdc87ae`).

Horizon native mods are compiled directly into the game and are **not sandboxed**. Only build source code you trust.

Horizon JEI reads the game's items and recipes, its container interface, chat, tooltips and screens. It writes only its own folder, `config/jei/` (`jei.cfg` for the options, `bookmarks.txt` for the bar), and nothing else. It makes no network connections.

*Unofficial project. Not affiliated with mezz, Mojang, Microsoft, or the Horizon project.*

The first playable Horizon JEI viewer, built on Horizon's native hook points (version 2).

### Item Browser & Search
- Added an item panel alongside container screens, displaying every item known to the game with pagination.
- Implemented JEI's search grammar:

  - `-exclusions` and `|` alternatives.
  - `@namespace` and `#tag` filters.

### Recipe & Usage Viewer
- Press **R** to view an item's recipes and **U** to view its uses.
- Works over the item panel and any slot in a container screen.
- Clicking an item in the panel opens the same views.

  - Furnace
  - Blast Furnace
  - Smoker
  - Campfire
  - Stonecutter
  - Smithing
  - Brewing

- Added a **Back** button to navigate through viewing history.
- Clicking a recipe slot opens that item's recipes.

### Recipe Placement
- Added the **+** button to place recipes into the open crafting grid when the recipe book contains them.
- The button remains disabled until the recipe is available in the recipe book.
- Shift-click is not supported yet because the panel's action event does not expose modifier keys.

- Added item giving through **Options → Mods → JEI** or `/jei give`.
- In creative mode, left-click gives one item and right-click gives a full stack.
- In survival mode, clicking an item opens its recipes instead.

### Localization & Diagnostics
- Added English and Spanish UI translations, configurable through the mod's **Language** setting.
- Item names are retrieved directly from the game and always respect the player's language.
- Added `/jei` to report the game's table sizes.

projects.summary: A camera that moves with you: it leans into strafes, sways on turns, dips on landing and bobs with your steps
projects.description:
A camera that moves with you. It leans into strafes, tips as you jump and fall, sways on fast turns, dips when you land, bobs with your steps and breathes while you stand still. Everything runs on springs, so the camera eases into each motion and settles back with a little weight instead of snapping.

- **Strafe and forward lean**: the camera rolls into sideways movement and tips slightly while running.
- **Turn sway**: fast mouse turns tilt the view.
- **Jump and fall tilt**: the view lifts going up and dips coming down.
- **Landing dip**: a hard landing bumps the camera down, then it springs back.
- **Step bob**: a soft bounce in step with your walking, on top of vanilla's.
- **Idle breathing** and **Speed FOV** (off by default).
- **Hand sway**: the held item lags behind fast turns and leans with the camera.

Every effect has its own strength (OFF to 200%), plus overall intensity, smoothness and bounce presets, how much stays while swimming or flying, when fast travel fades it out (elytra, boats, minecarts, so it stays out of flight mods' way) and the lean direction. All in Options > Mods > Living Camera, with a key to toggle it in game.

Client side only: it works in single player and on any server. It reads only your own position, view and the block at your eyes, with no network or file access beyond its own settings.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/living-camera

Inspired by Camera Overhaul by Mirsario (https://github.com/Mirsario/Minecraft-CameraOverhaul). Written from scratch for Horizon: it contains none of Camera Overhaul's code or assets and is not made or endorsed by Mirsario.

projects.name: Lumina
projects.summary: High performance with real-time shadows, physical water, roof overhang occlusion, volumetric 3D clouds, and sharp anti-aliasing
projects.description:
Native shaders designed for high frame rates and clean, balanced visuals without post-processing blur. All options are fully configurable directly in the shader settings menu.

**Lighting & Overhang Shading**
- Balanced daytime lighting with warm sun and clean azure shadows.
- Directional sky dome occlusion: accurate contrast between ground, walls, and ceilings.
- Non-linear ambient occlusion under house roofs, eaves, porches, and balconies.
- Selective midtone vibrance on grass and foliage without clipping bright highlights.
- Foliage subsurface scattering and sun-facing rim lighting.

**Shadows**
- Real-time sun and moon shadow maps with distortion-aware filtering.
- Acne-free shadows on terrain, blocks, and thin grass at any distance.
- Selectable shadow map resolution: 512, 1024, 1536, or 2048.

**Clarity Anti-Aliasing (FXAA)**
- Edge-selective geometric smoothing on block silhouettes, roofs, and stairs.
- Flat surfaces, textures, wood, stone, and UI remain 100% sharp with zero blurring.
- Modes: Sharp, Smooth, or Off.

**Water & Underwater**
- High-speed Screen Space Reflections (SSR) combined with planar mirror reflections.
- Physics-based Beer-Lambert light absorption with depth-dependent color transition.
- Snell's window when looking up from underwater with total internal reflection.
- Animated seabed caustics, wave refraction, and underwater depth fog.

**Clouds & Atmosphere**
- Raymarched procedural 3D cumulus clouds with Fast, Balanced, and Cinematic presets.
- Volumetric god rays through terrain and trees.
- Procedural rain puddles on grass and dirt with raindrop impact ripples.
- Custom weather rendering for rain and snow particles.
- Native block emission and dynamic colored lighting support.

**Setup Note:**
Set Clouds to OFF in your video settings to let the custom 3D clouds render properly.

projects.name: Menu Panorama
projects.summary: Put your own wallpaper behind the main menu in Horizon — Minecraft 26.3, rewritten in Rust.
projects.description:
Menu Panorama is a resource pack for **Horizon** — Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, rewritten from scratch in **Rust**.

It replaces the six textures of the main-menu background with a picture you choose. It is a plain resource pack, not a Java mod: no mod loader, no Java, and no code from the pack is executed. Horizon loads it natively.

- **Any photo** in the `room` mode: the picture is shown whole on the four walls, with mirrored seams and soft colours above and below.
- **A 360° equirectangular panorama** in the `360` mode: the sphere is cut into six cube faces, so the view stays seamless when the camera turns.
- **Auto** picks the mode from the image's aspect ratio.

Build a pack in the browser with `panorama-maker.html`: drop an image, choose a face size, download the `.zip`. Everything runs locally; the picture never leaves the computer. `make_panorama.py` does the same from the command line.

The pack only changes `assets/minecraft/textures/gui/title/background/panorama_0..5.png`; gameplay, sounds and other textures are untouched. `pack.mcmeta` is made for Horizon 26.3 (resource format 97) and also declares formats 15–999, so the same file loads in Minecraft Java 1.21+. A demo pack is attached to every release.

MIT licensed. Source, the browser generator and the CLI are in the repository.

projects.description:
An adaptive minimap and a full world map for Horizon, with a shared in-memory terrain cache.

- Minimap in four corners, square or round, 64–256 GUI pixels, 0.1–4 blocks per pixel, and optional player rotation.

- Hover shows the pointed-at coordinates, the localised biome and waypoint names; the hovered block is outlined.

- Separate waypoint manager (N by default) for creating, renaming and deleting waypoints; waypoints are drawn as first-letter markers on the HUD through walls and on both maps.

projects.description:
Bright, colorful shader pack for Horizon. Horizon had no shaders on the registry, so I made one. Style is close to Complementary Reimagined, but the code is mine, written from scratch in WGSL.

## What you get

- **Soft shadows.** Sun and moon cast them. Water and stained glass tint the light that goes through.
- **Sky and fog match.** Blue day, orange sunsets, dark blue night. Far terrain fades into the sky, no hard line at the horizon.
- **Colored light.** Torches are warm, soul fire is blue, redstone is red, sea lanterns are cyan, amethyst is purple.

- **Nether and End look different.** Nether is hot and hazy, with heat shimmer. End is cold and purple.

- Shadow quality: Low
- Water reflections: off
- Bloom: off
- Shadows: off. Biggest gain.

- Horizon shader API is 0.1, experimental. It can change.
- Entities, block entities and particles are not shaded yet. There is no stage for them.

projects.name: Motion Blur
projects.summary: Blurs what moves: mobs, players, items and vehicles along their own motion, with optional camera blur.
projects.description:
Moving mobs, players, items, minecarts and boats blur along their own motion. The camera's motion (turning, walking) can blur too, and is off by default.

Each frame the mod works out every pixel's motion since the last frame (the world's from the depth buffer and the camera, entities from last frame's vertices), finds the largest motion near each tile, and gathers along it with depth-aware weights (McGuire et al., "A Reconstruction Filter for Plausible Motion Blur", 2012).

Settings are in Options → Mods → Motion Blur: strength for moving things and the camera, shutter angle or a fixed exposure, the longest blur, quality, blurring yourself in third person, and a view that shows each pixel's motion.

projects.name: Movement Status
projects.summary: Better toggle Sprint/Sneak display functionality
projects.description:
# Movement Status

A lightweight native HUD for Horizon that shows your current movement state in the corner of the screen.

It reads the live player state (sprinting, sneaking, flying, elytra gliding) and the physical vs. logical key state so it can correctly distinguish between a key that is being held and a key that is toggled via vanilla’s Toggle Sprint / Toggle Crouch options.

## Features

- Live movement status in the bottom-left corner:
  - `Sprint [Held]` / `Sprint [Toggled]`
  - `Sneak [Held]` / `Sneak [Toggled]`
  - `Flying [Creative]` / `Flying [Elytra]`
- Multiple states can be shown at once (sprint + sneak, etc.)
- Optional semi-transparent background box
- Respects vanilla Toggle Sprint and Toggle Crouch settings
- Uses the real physical key state so the Held/Toggled labels stay accurate

## Requirements

- Horizon (Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3)
- Native mod support enabled in the launcher

## Installation

1. Install the mod from the launcher’s Mods page (or drop the `.hnmod` into `horizon-native-mods/`).
2. Click **Build** and confirm the native-code warning.
3. Once built, turn the mod on under Options → Mods.

## Settings

A single toggle controls the background box. Open Options → Mods → Movement Status → Settings to turn it on or off.

## Notes

This is a status HUD only. It does not change movement, keybinds, or gameplay. It simply reports what the game is already doing.

The physical key checks currently use the vanilla defaults (Left Control for sprint, Left Shift for sneak). Custom keybinds may show the wrong Held/Toggled label until a future update maps the bound key.

## License

MIT

projects.description:
An original shader pack written in Horizon's own WGSL shader format (shader API 0.1).

- **Painted sky**: the gradient changes through the day, with a pink band at sunrise and sunset and a halo around the sun.
- **Clouds**: sunlit cumulus with self-shadowing, glowing edges against the light and darker bases, high cirrus, and a full overcast during storms.
- **Night**: twinkling stars that turn with the sky, a faint nebula, and auroras in cold biomes.
- **Shadows**: crisp, stable shadows from the sun and moon, tinted by the water and stained glass they pass through; clouds cast shadows on the ground.
- **Water**: turquoise (emerald in the shallows, deep teal further out) or biome colors, a living swell that never repeats, sun glitter, and reflections that ripple with the surface. Under it, light loses its red then its green with depth, and caustics dance on the bed.

- **Wind**: grass, flowers, leaves and vines sway; underwater, a current rocks the seagrass and kelp.
- **Atmosphere and image**: light shafts, haze that matches the sky, ambient occlusion, bloom, adaptive exposure, color grading, vignette and anti-aliasing.

Every effect can be tuned from the pack's menu.

## Install

Put `nimbe.hshader` in the game's `shaderpacks` folder (the **Open Pack Folder** button opens it), then pick **Nimbe** in Options > Video Settings > Shaders > Shader Packs.

## Performance

The most expensive settings, in order: shadows and their resolution, water reflections, light shafts, cloud quality. On a small GPU, start with a shadow resolution of 1024 and light shafts on Low.

All the code is original and not taken from any other shader pack.

projects.name: Orbital Laser
projects.summary: Fifteen orbital strikes, from a laser to a Planet Killer: a designator, a wheel, and craters that stay.
projects.description:
By Stink-O. Orbital Laser adds an Orbital Laser Designator. Aim it and hold right-click to call down one of fifteen orbital strikes (hold it and press R for the laser wheel, or type `/orbital wheel`), each with its own sky, sound and scar: the Orbital Laser, the Godly Laser, a Black Hole, the Meteor Storm, the Mothership, the Downfall, the Planet Killer, the Crystal Bloom, the Sinkhole, the Payload, the Nuke, the Rod from God, the Supercell, the Hurricane and the Tsunami. The wheel also sets your creative flying speed and the strike's approach, arrival and colours.

**Read before you fire**

- **Terrain damage is permanent.** A strike flattens and digs out the land, up to hundreds of blocks across, and kills the mobs and dropped items nearby (not players). Use a throwaway world. `/orbital terrain off` (or the wheel's centre) makes strikes light and sound only.
- **Photosensitivity.** The Rod from God has ~0.17 s of stark impact frames as it strikes, and several strikes (the Planet Killer, the Hurricane and the Supercell among them) have lightning and flashes, and the Tsunami's blow, as the water takes you, is one white flash over the whole picture. `/orbital impactframes off` (the wheel's IMPACT FX switch) turns the impact frames off. If flashing light affects you, skip those strikes.
- **Big strikes are heavy.** QUALITY FAST (the default) draws the smoke at half size; `/orbital quality full` for the full look.

**Native mod.** The mod's code is compiled into the game, runs with the access the game has to your computer, and is not sandboxed, so install it only if you trust it. The launcher shows its trust notice and waits for you to press Build; the first native build downloads the launcher's Rust and takes 20 to 30 minutes. Pick **Release build** on the Native build row first: it builds more slowly, but the game runs noticeably faster. It builds on the Horizon revision it was tested on, whatever Nightly you have.

What each system needs first:

- **Linux** (x86-64), tested: a C compiler, `pkg-config` and the ALSA and libudev development files (Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libasound2-dev libudev-dev`); the launcher names what is missing.
- **Windows** (x64), build-checked, not yet played: nothing; the launcher brings its own Rust and MinGW-w64.
- **macOS** (Apple Silicon), build-checked, not yet played: Apple's Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`).
- **macOS** (Intel): not available; the launcher can't build native mods there.

**One file for code and content.** The game reads content mods only from `horizon-mods/`, so this mod carries a small mixin (`content_find`, on `horizon_mods::manifest::find`) that has the game read its content (`horizon-mod.toml`, `assets/`, `data/`) from its own `horizon-native-mods/orbital.hnmod` too. It writes and copies nothing, and steps aside when a content mod `orbital` is already in `horizon-mods/`. It goes away once the game reads content from native files (horizon-rust/horizon#5865).

Known issues:

- On Macs the Downfall's effects don't draw: Apple's Metal compiler fails on its pass, so you get its land and sound but not its visuals. Every other strike drew on the Macs it was tried on.
- Multiplayer and LAN haven't been tested on the native build; it's made for single player. On a server or LAN host, only a level 4 operator can fire strikes that change the world.
- Each new version rebuilds the game (the first build 20 to 30 minutes, later ones quicker), unlike a plain mod.

Items, models, textures and sounds are the mod's own: nothing from Minecraft is in it. An independent fan project, not affiliated with Mojang, Microsoft or the Horizon project. Source, screenshots, how it works and the full command list: https://github.com/Stink-O/orbital-laser

projects.name: SeedCrackerX
projects.summary: SeedCrackerX for Horizon: finds the world seed of a server from the structures you walk past, outlined through walls.
projects.description:
A port to Rust of [SeedCrackerX](https://github.com/19MisterX98/SeedcrackerX) 2.16.2 for Horizon, written from the Java source together with the parts of the SeedFinding libraries it calls. Walk near structures (igloos, temples, monuments, shipwrecks, end cities, buried treasure, outposts, trial chambers, desert wells, end gateways, emerald ore, dungeons) and they are outlined through walls; with enough of them the world seed is printed in chat. Commands are `/seedcracker ...` as in the Java (`render outlines`, `finder`, `data`, `cracker`, `version`, `database`, `gui`), and the settings are on the mod's page in Options > Mods. PARITY.md in the source lists every Java file and what became of it.

What it does not do: the Dungeon and Warped Fungus cracking of Minecraft 1.17 and older (it needs a lattice solver) and the biome-based world seed search. A world seed is found from structures and the hashed seed the server sends. Like the Java mod it shows information the game does not draw by itself, so some servers do not allow it: that choice is the player's.

For reviewers:
- Network, in two places, both in `src/game/seedcracker.rs` and both the Java mod's own behaviour: (1) once when the mod starts, one HTTP GET of the public Google Sheet of known server seeds (`DATABASE_URL`, `src/config/database.rs`) on a background thread, always, with no switch; (2) only if the player switches `databaseSubmits` on (off by default), when a seed is cracked on a server with more than 10 players: the mod asks the game's own `horizon_client::auth::join_server` to prove the account to Mojang's session service under the id `seedcrackerx`, then posts the server address, dimension, seed, version and the player's name (or a hash of it) to the sheet's script (`DATABASE_POST_URL`). The mod never reads or stores the access token. Nothing else opens a socket.
- It writes only under `horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/seedcrackerx/`: `seedcracker.json` (settings, the Java's layout), `known_seeds.txt` and a folder `SeedCracker saved structures`; it reads the same files back.
- It starts an operating system program in one place, `open_uri` in `src/game/seedcracker.rs` (`rundll32` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux): `/seedcracker database` and the links on its settings page open the seed sheet in the browser.
- The `.hnmod` is built from the source of the tagged release, `python tools/pack.py`, and is the same file every time (line endings are written as LF). It carries `LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`.
- MIT, like every original it is a port of; `NOTICE.md` lists SeedCrackerX and the SeedFinding libraries it calls with their copyright notices. Tests: `cargo test` (a diff against 7.3k lines produced by the real Java libraries, the cracker, the finders).
- Pinned to Nightly 2026-11-04 (6475f62): the launcher builds the game on that commit, and so does not depend on the Nightly the player has.
authors: luhnox (this port); SeedCrackerX by 19MisterX98 and the SeedCrackerX contributors; the SeedFinding libraries by KaptainWutax and Neil and Matthew Bolan

projects.name: Serverify
projects.summary: Find Minecraft servers and add them to your Multiplayer list, from a page in your web browser.
projects.description:
Serverify is a server browser. Press **F8** (or type `/serverify web`, or press the button on the mod's settings page) and your web browser opens a page with a search box, a category menu and cards showing each server's picture, address, player count and country. Press **Add** and the server goes to the top of your Multiplayer list. Then join it from Horizon's own Multiplayer screen.

It is the Horizon version of [Serverify](https://github.com/Louchatfroff/serverify), the server browser for Fabric, Quilt, Forge and NeoForge, by the same author.

## What it does

- Opens a server browser page in your web browser: search, 22 categories, an offline-mode filter and an **Add** button.
- Adds servers to `servers.dat` in the game folder, with the name cleaned of colour codes.
- Adds chat commands: `/serverify web`, `list [category]`, `search <words>`, `next`, `prev`, `add <number>` and `categories`.
- Adds a row in Options > Mods with a rebindable key (F8 by default) and a settings page with two buttons: open the browser, and **Offline-mode servers only** (on by default).

Horizon joins servers that check Minecraft accounts with your Microsoft sign-in, like the official launcher. This version still turns the offline-mode filter on by default, from a time when Horizon couldn't: turn it off to see all servers.

## What it contacts

- **Modrinth.** The game asks `api.modrinth.com` for the server list and `cdn.modrinth.com` for server pictures, only when you look for servers.
- **Three listing sites.** With the offline-mode filter off (and for top-mc-servers.net's list of cracked servers when it is on), the game fetches public pages of `top-mc-servers.net`, `minecraftservers.org` and `minecraft-mp.com`, and their server pictures. The game builds those addresses itself. The page reads the fetched pages with the browser's own HTML parser.
- **A page on your computer.** The first time you open the page, the mod starts a small web server on `127.0.0.1` (this computer only, never the network) with a random secret in its address, made for each session. The page talks only to that server. A request with another host name, another origin or no secret is refused. The server can show the list, send a picture and add one server to your Multiplayer list.
- It sends no data about you, and makes no request at any other time.

## What it does not do

- It does not run any code from the sites it reads, and it does not send your data anywhere.
- It does not change anything but `servers.dat` (one entry at a time) and its own settings in `horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/serverify/`.
- It does not draw screens or buttons in the game: Horizon's hook points have none, so the screen is your web browser.
- It cannot make Horizon join servers that check Minecraft accounts.
- Adding a server rewrites `servers.dat`, which drops the hidden direct-join entries Horizon keeps. Your saved servers stay.

## Install

Install it from the launcher's Mods page, then press Build there, and play that instance. Guide: https://github.com/Louchatfroff/serverify/tree/main/horizon/serverify#readme

Native mods are not sandboxed. The source is public and licensed GPL-3.0-only: https://github.com/Louchatfroff/serverify/tree/main/horizon/serverify

projects.description:

1. Go to https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard and press **Create app**.

- `/music volume [0-100] | play | pause | next | previous | shuffle | repeat | hide | position | restart | logout`
- Keys for next, previous, play/pause and hiding the box in Options → Mods → Spotify HUD (unbound by default).

Settings, the login and `theme.json` (colours you can edit) are in `horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/spotify_hud/`.

projects.description:
**Trails** leaves a trail behind you as you move. Only you see it: nothing is sent to the server or to other players.

- **Cat paws**: alternating paw prints on the blocks you walk on. They follow the local light and vanish when the block under them is removed or changes height.
- **Particle**: sparkles, dust, orbs or hearts drifting behind you.
- **Line**: a thin line along your path.
- **Ribbon**: a flat ribbon along your path.

Trails fade after a few seconds, or stay in persistent mode (bounded in memory, never saved into the world). Changing mode, dimension or world clears them.

**Controls**
- **K** turns trails on and off (rebind it in Options > Mods > Trails).
- **Options > Mods > Trails > Settings**: mode, colours, sizes, spacing, opacity, glow, rainbow, fade times and render distance.

**What it does and doesn't do**: it reads your position, the blocks under you and the light level, draws in the world, and saves its settings in `horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/trails/`. It makes no network connections and doesn't change gameplay, the world or any other files.

projects.summary: Talk with Simple Voice Chat players: proximity voice, groups, push to talk and a menu (V).
projects.description:
An unofficial client for the [Simple Voice Chat](https://github.com/henkelmax/simple-voice-chat) protocol. On a server with the Simple Voice Chat mod or plugin, you can talk with players who use the Java mod on the regular launcher.

## What it does

- **Menu (V):** connection status, microphone and voice chat on/off, push to talk or voice activation, voice volume, microphone gain and activation level with a live meter, and every hotkey as it is bound now. The right side lists the server's groups with their members: join (with a password if needed), leave, or create a group.
- **Talking:** hold Caps Lock (push to talk) or use voice activation. Voices come from where players stand, getting quieter with distance and panned left or right.
- **Groups:** each player's group shows above their head. `/vc join <group> [password]`, `/vc leave`, `/vc create <name> [password] [normal|open|isolated]` and `/vc groups` work too.
- **Keys** (Options > Mods > Horizon Voice Chat): menu (V), push to talk (Caps Lock), whisper (unbound), mute (J), voice chat off/on (K).
- **Protocols:** Simple Voice Chat 2.6.x (compatibility 20) and 2.7 (21).

## What it touches

- It reads the server's `voicechat:*` custom payloads and other players' positions inside `game::remote`, so it is pinned to Horizon `c9d474d`.
- It opens one UDP connection to the server's voice chat port, encrypted with AES-128-GCM using the secret the server sends.
- It uses the default microphone and speakers through cpal, and loads the system **libopus** at run time (the `opus` package must be installed).
- It keeps its settings in Horizon's own mod settings. It contacts no host other than the Minecraft server you are on (and DNS, for the server's SRV record).

## Not affiliated

This project is not made, endorsed or supported by Max Henkel or the Simple Voice Chat project. It contains none of Simple Voice Chat's code: everything is written from scratch in Rust.

## Tested

The engine's unit tests pass, and the modded client type-checks. Live, against Paper 26.3 with the Simple Voice Chat 2.6.27 plugin, it authenticated and connected, a test tone was heard through the server, and groups and labels came from the server. Not tested yet: the menu in the real game, a real microphone, 2.7 servers, and talking with the Java mod itself.

projects.name: Waymap
projects.summary: Persistent client-side waypoints with 3D world markers, minimap dots, a native editor, and automatic death markers for Horizon.
projects.description:
Waymap brings complete waypoint management into the game itself. Instead of relying only on chat commands or external tools, it provides a native Horizon screen for creating, finding and editing waypoints, while keeping the existing /wp commands and minimap behaviour. Waypoints are stored locally per world or server, survive restarts, and never require server-side installation. Deaths are recorded automatically so the player can always find the place where they died.
Features
- World markers — 3D waypoints projected from the player's camera, hidden when outside the view
- Minimap markers — coloured dots at the correct map position, including rotated maps
- Native waypoint screen — list and editor with mouse and keyboard support
- Filters — All, Overworld, Nether, End and Deaths
- Editor — name, X/Y/Z, current position, dimension, 16-colour palette, visibility
- Automatic death waypoints — every death creates Death 1, Death 2, … at the death spot, drawn as a red X
- HUD panel — optional bottom-left list with the nearest waypoints and distances
- Full command suite — /wp commands remain available alongside the GUI
- Per-context storage — separate files for each singleplayer world and multiplayer server
- Atomic persistence — temporary file plus atomic rename; unreadable files are never overwritten
- Legacy migration — old waypoints.txt files are migrated once, with waypoints.txt.v1.bak preserved
- Whole coordinates — all waypoint coordinates are rounded to whole numbers
- Settings and rebindable keys — markers, labels, HUD panel, create key and list key
- Up to 512 waypoints per context
Usage
Keys
- N — create a waypoint at the current position
- B or M — open or close the waypoint list
- Esc — close the list or cancel the editor
- Enter — save the editor or edit the selected waypoint
- Tab / Shift+Tab — next or previous editor field
- ↑ / ↓ — move the list selection or editor field
- PgUp / PgDn / Home / End — navigate the list
- Delete — clear the focused editor field; twice on the list deletes the row
GUI
Click a row to select it. The list offers filter buttons, Hide/Show, Edit, Delete, + New and Close; the mouse wheel scrolls. The editor provides name, X/Y/Z, Use my position, dimension cycling, colour palette, visibility and save/cancel.
Commands
- /wp add [name] — add a waypoint at the current position
- /wp del <name> — delete a waypoint
- /wp list — list waypoints in the current context
- /wp rename <old> <new> — rename a waypoint
- /wp color <name> <color> — set a colour by name or #rrggbb
- /wp clear — delete all waypoints in the current context
- /wp edit <name> — show waypoint information
- /wp hide <name> — hide a waypoint from the world and minimap
- /wp show <name> — show a hidden waypoint
- /wp help — show the command list

projects.description:

Press **X** to see ores through the world, as a native mod for Horizon.

While it is on, every block except ores (coal, copper, iron, gold, redstone, lapis, diamond, emerald, their
deepslate kinds, nether gold and quartz, ancient debris), chests, spawners, water and lava is drawn as air, and what is left shines at full brightness. Press X again to see the world as usual. Rebind the key in
Options > Mods.

Single player only: it turns itself off as soon as the world is no longer a closed single player world, so it does
not work on servers or in a world opened to LAN.

projects.name: Zoom
projects.summary: Hold a key to zoom in; the mouse wheel zooms further while you hold it.
projects.description:
Horizon's own zoom, formerly an extra in Options > Horizon Extras.

- Hold the key (Z by default) to zoom in at the starting zoom; let go and the view comes back.
- While you hold it, the mouse wheel zooms further in or out (up to 10x) and the hotbar stays put.
- Smooth zoom eases in and out like the spyglass; slower turning keeps aiming steady.
- Settings: Options > Mods > Zoom > Settings (the key; starting zoom; smooth zoom; slower turning).

It hears its own key and the mouse wheel while you hold it, and zooms the camera: nothing else.

Now a native mod (2.0.0): built into the game by the launcher, on the Horizon you play, like any native mod
(install it on the launcher's Mods page, then press Build there). Your settings carry over from 1.0.0. Turn it off in
Options > Mods: it rests at once, and the next build leaves it out. Its source is
[horizon-mods/native/zoom](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon-mods/tree/main/native/zoom).

versions.changelog: Native: built into the game by the launcher on Horizon's native hook points; settings carry over; turn it off in Options > Mods.

projects.name: Zoomify
projects.summary: A port of Zoomify: a zoom key with smooth transitions, scroll zoom, a secondary zoom and Zoomify's own settings screen.
projects.description:
A port of [Zoomify](https://github.com/isXander/Zoomify) by isXander to Horizon, as a native mod.

- **Zoom** (C, hold or toggle) with Zoomify's transitions, times and initial zoom; **scroll zoom** with the mouse wheel while zooming; the **secondary zoom** (F6), slow and cinematic, that hides the HUD.
- Relative sensitivity, the cinematic camera while zooming, the hand's field of view and the **spyglass** rules (combine, override, only while holding or carrying it; its overlay and sounds).
- **Zoomify's own config screen**, as in Java (YACL): Mod Menu's Configure button, Options > Mods > Zoomify > Configure..., or `/zoomify`. Tabs, collapsible groups, sliders and reset buttons, the description panel with Zoomify's animated demo pictures, search, Undo / Reset / Save, and the presets (Default, OptiFine, OK Zoomer). English and Russian.

Built for Horizon Nightly 2026-11-08 (`fdc87ae`). Native mods are compiled into the game and are not sandboxed: build only code you trust.

**Credits.** Zoomify is Copyright (C) isXander, licensed under the GNU LGPL 3.0 or later; this port keeps that licence and is not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft.

projects.name: Better+

projects.description: Better+ is the pack we recommend first. There are lamps, industrial blocks, all 179 Macaw's trapdoors and Silent's Gems underground. It adds conveniences and decoration, not a different game. 39 mods, one pin, one click.

projects.description: Studio is built for recording. projects.summary: AE2, Create, Voltz, ProjectE, a quarry and gems in one pack. Three pins; the first build takes a while.
projects.description: The Works puts the technical half of the registry into one pack. AE2 handles storage and autocrafting, Create handles mechanics, Voltz handles power and reactors, ProjectE handles EMC, Deepbore Quarry feeds the machines and Silent's Gems stocks the ore shelf. JEI and Jade explain what you're looking at, and sorting keeps the terminals usable. It pins three Horizon commits, so expect one Build anyway prompt and a slower first build. Twenty mods, not five hundred.

Light Overlay shows where mobs can spawn and MineLights gives you a lamp you can place in a hurry. There are no ME networks or factories: a pickaxe, a quarry and a chest.

Enchantment Hints explains what an enchantment does, and two extra recipes patch the most annoying gaps in vanilla crafting. No bosses, no timers.

Spider-Man adds web swinging, zips and wall running tuned against the console games, while trails, a living camera and speed blur add the sense of speed. The HUD stays out of the way.

Server Flags shows where a server lives, RMotd rotates the MOTD, and Cross Version with ViaHorizon opens older protocols for offline-mode servers. projects.description: Cockpit is an interface pack with a rule: each piece of information gets one home. HUD+ is the only editor, with drag-and-drop placement, four views per module and a PvP profile. Beautiful Day Counter adds a clock; Keystrokes, FPS Counter, Held Item Info, Item New, Spotify HUD and Rider HUD fill the corners. Mouse Tricks and InventoryWizard handle the inventory, SmartF3 tidies the debug screen, and LookAt and Map Preview explain the world. AppleSkin, Armor Status and Status Effect HUD are left out because HUD+ draws them already.

projects.summary: Dark caves, physics and blood: a survival pack that makes the night matter again.
projects.description: Blackout makes vanilla feel less forgiving. Maps, light overlay, fullbright and coordinates are gone, so a cave is dark and a torch is worth carrying. PhysicsModHorizon gives water that never repeats and ragdolls instead of vanishing mobs; Visuality adds pixel particles, Blood Particles adds impact, and motion blur and a living camera add speed. The HUD is cut to armour and the held item. Difficulty stays on vanilla hardcore: the pack adds weight, not bigger numbers.
